To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a multiscale segmentation can be obtained using a hierarchy of graph cuts.
a good segmentation should be consistent with grouping cues at multiple scales and that the average of normalized affinity cuts is a good criterion to achieve this.

(a) edges at multiple scales provide reliable grouping cues for image analysis; (b) a multiscale edge can be represented as a multiscale graph, which can be used for simultaneous segmentation of all the scales; (c) a novel criterion called average cut of normalized affinity is used for evaluating the segmentation of all the graphs, which leads to the simultaneous segmentation of the multiscale graphs; (d) this approach leads to a natural coarse-to-fine segmentation that is able to handle textured regions
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to use multiscale cues to segment images and how to design efficient algorithms to solve this problem.
how to integrate multiple scales of grouping cues for better segmentations.
how to combine multiple cues at multiple scales to achieve a good segmentation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our multiscale graph-cuts approach is a good segmentation method.
the proposed approach provides a principled way to combine multiscale cues for image segmentation.
this paper presents an efficient and effective algorithm for simultaneous segmentation of images at multiple scales.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a multiscale framework for image segmentation.
we have developed a novel graph-cuts approach to image segmentation that can be used in a multiscale fashion, and that can be applied to images of arbitrary size.
we propose a new criterion for simultaneous segmentation of images using multiscale cues and develop an efficient graph-cuts approach for finding its near-global optimum.
The main takeaway from our work is that
multiscale grouping cues are complementary, and their integration leads to a better segmentation.
multiscale cues are complementary to one another and should not be discarded.
a multiscale segmentation can be achieved in a principled manner by simultaneously optimizing over multiple grids.
